the fleets of the Christian Powers of Europe. If it were not for these same Christian Powers Crete would Tao. be a province of Greece end there would be an end of the long centurien of martyr- dom it has suffered under Turkish rule. Yet the six Christian Powers are not matistied with ties connummation. They appear to !le determined to out-Herod Herod. It in said that even the HULT.iIf himself would now be glad to let the Cretans go. He evidently thinks that Christian subjects who will not allow themselves to be quietly outraged and murdered are a cause of weaknem and not of atrength to his Empire. But the six Christian Powers aro more Turkish than the SULTAN himself. They have decided that Crete must remain a Turkish dependency. The object upon which they are now concentrating their energien is the expulsion of the Greeks. If they get their own way, the Greeks must go but the Turks will remain, in order, says Lord Haus- bray, to discharge the dutiee of policemen !In plain words. men of the same type as those who perpetrated the atrocities in Armenia and Conntantineple are to be installed, under the auspices of the Christian Power., as police- men in a community which in numbers is overwhelmingly Christian. That is the level to which the etateemanehip of Europe—Eng- lard included—has descended. Is it to be won- dered at, therefore, that the people of Greece indignantly refuse to comply with the demands that are ~ado npon them. They decline to with- draw their soldiers from Crete AO long an the Turks are loft in possession. The Tiestion now is, will the Powers proceed to enforce their dornewlm upon Greece by force % That is a question which will be answered by "events within a few days and perhaps a few humro. The three emperors of Russia, Germaiy and Austria are evidently deter- mined to stop at nothing in the way of coercion, but what action will be taken by England, France end Italy, whose governments are influ- enced by public opinion Tiler° are reasons for believing that the boy te the position lies with Lord SALI.O.IIII. The people of France and Italy are dead agninnt coercion, lost if England thrown itself on the side of the Emperors the govern- ments of those countries will find it aimed im- poseible to withdraw from the Concert of Europe. A great renponsibility therefore rests with Lord SALINBURY. In synepathy,the English people ere almost entirely with the Greeks, and if English ships are used for coercive oilmen., practically at the bidding of the autocrats ot Eerope, there will be • display of public indigreitien the repel of which he. not beau soon sine., the days of the Bulgarian agitation.
